body:
Sources such as https://www.forbes.com/sites/zakdoffman/2024/12/18/feds-warn-android-and-iphone-users-stop-using-sms-for-2fa/ report that the US Gov't is advising to fully stop using SMS for secure communication and SMS. I suggest we change:

| # | Description | 
| :---: | :--- |
| **2.7.1** | [MODIFIED] Verify that authentication mechanisms using the Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN) to deliver One-time Passwords (OTPs) via phone or SMS are offered only when alternate stronger methods (such as push notifications) are also offered and when the service provides information on their security risks to users. |  

.. to ..

| # | Description | 
| :---: | :--- | 
| **2.7.1** | [MODIFIED] Verify that authentication mechanisms using the Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN) to deliver One-time Passwords (OTPs) via phone or SMS are not allowed. |

comments.body: This is a very big change and I do not take this suggestion lightly. Would others like to chime in? cc @randomstuff ?

I understand the reasons why the US government is advising to fully stop using SMS and I don't disagree. However,

* maybe this is not such a big deal to still rely on SMS for casual applications (?);
* in practice, this is still used a *lot* so I am wondering whether this requirement is really realistic (we can argue that we don't have to care about that).

I have some arguments on this topic but I don't have an opinion.

Using SMS for high risks apps in Europe is fairly unheard of. The US gov’t is trying to push US companies in the same direction and if we are ok about being progressive, I support this change.

Maybe we want this to be split level. Ok for L1 but not ok for L2/L3. I hesitate to suggest a split-level requirement but maybe it’s needed here.

It looks like 2.7.1 will be an L2 requirement. We could try a split requirement here. What do we think about:

| # | Description | 
| :---: | :--- |
| **2.7.1** | [MODIFIED] Verify that authentication mechanisms using the Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN) to deliver One-time Passwords (OTPs) via phone or SMS are offered only when alternate stronger methods (such as push notifications) are also offered and when the service provides information on their security risks to users. **For L3 applications, phone and SMS should not be available options.** |  

@elarlang ?
